key_insight: The paper argues that polymer informatics is ready to evolve from isolated prediction tools into a modular, agentic super-intelligence that can interpret design goals, coordinate specialized models, and support end-to-end polymer discovery.
engineering_relevance: For computational materials engineering, this roadmap points toward AI systems that can accelerate inverse design, synthesis planning, process selection, and performance optimization across polymers, composites, solvents, and formulations.
method: Proposes a modular agent-directed architecture that maps a natural-language research question to domain-specific tools.
Covers the full design chain from molecular generation and property prediction to synthesis feasibility and practicality assessment.
Positions autonomous closed-loop experimentation as the remaining major step toward a self-driving polymer laboratory.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites experience building two complementary agentic and informatics platforms and surveys demonstrated capabilities across literature data extraction, chemistry-aware representation, property prediction, solvent recommendation, and retrosynthetic planning.
watch_item: The vision is still limited by gaps in autonomous closed-loop experimentation and by the need to match tools reliably to available data across diverse polymer classes and tasks.
paper_title: A roadmap for polymer informatics super-intelligence
